prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right choice depends on your goals (talking-head avatar vs product clip vs scalable ad variants), budget, and how much creative control you want. Below are the top options by use case plus a quick checklist to choose the best one for you.

Top picks by use case

- Talking‑head / spokesperson-style ads (AI avatars)
  - Synthesia — best for polished, enterprise‑grade AI presenters and many languages. Pros: realistic avatars, script → video, easy localization. Cons: pricier, less cinematic editing.
  - HeyGen / Movio — similar to Synthesia; often more affordable and fast iteration.

- Turn long content into short social ads / repurposing
  - Pictory — excellent at converting blog posts/long videos into short clips with captions and templates.

- Template-driven social ads / marketers who want speed
  - InVideo — lots of ad templates, easy drag‑and‑drop, affordable plans; good for quick Facebook/Instagram/TikTok creatives.
  - Promo.com — strong asset library and ad templates built specifically for marketing use.

- Scalable ad variations / e‑commerce & performance marketing
  - Shakr — built for scalable Meta/IG ad creation and variants.
  - Smartly.io (plus creative tools) — more ad-ops focused; pairs creative production with ad deployment/optimization.

- Advanced creative & generative video
  - Runway — powerful generative tools (text-to-video, background replacement) for more creative/visual ads; steeper learning curve.

- Precise editing / voice cloning / screen + explainer ads
  - Descript — excellent for editing, overdub voice cloning, captions, and simple screen-recorded ads.

- All-around, browser-based with useful AI features
  - VEED — good balance of auto-subtitles, templates, and some generative features for social ads.

What to consider when choosing
- Primary ad format and platform (30s YouTube, 15s Instagram Reel, TikTok creative).
- Need for AI avatars or real footage.
- Speed vs custom look (templates = fast, custom editing = slower).
- Multilingual capability and localization tools.
- Ability to produce many variants (dynamic creative/ad personalization).
- Budget and licensing (royalty-free/commercial use).
- Export quality (1080/4K), aspect ratios, native ad specs.
- Collaboration/team features and integrations with ad platforms.
- Trial availability and hidden costs (per‑video fees, extra voices, avatar credits).

How to pick and test quickly
1. Pick 2–3 candidates from above.
2. Use their free trial or lowest plan to make one ad (same script/visual brief).
3. Compare speed, cost, quality (voice + lip sync, caption accuracy, editing ease).
4. Run A/B test in a small ad spend to measure real performance.

If you tell me: platform (Facebook/Instagram/TikTok/YouTube), ad length, budget, whether you want AI avatars or product footage, and how many variants you need, I’ll recommend the best 2–3 specific tools and one starter workflow.
